name: Motorcycle
description: Every motor vehicle with a seat or saddle for the rider designed to travel on no more than three wheels. A seated electric two-wheeler past the electric-assisted bicycle limits is one, since New Mexico's moped category covers only small combustion engines. Defined by NMSA 1978 §66-1-4.11, as amended by SB 69 (2023).
restrictions: A seat or saddle for the rider, and no more than three wheels on the ground
An electric moped-class vehicle is a motorcycle because the moped definition requires a piston engine under 50 cc
A two- or three-wheeler that can exceed 20 mph on electric power alone and isn't an electric-assisted bicycle is also an electric mobility device
Riders need a Class M license; it's available from 13 with the Motorcycle Safety Foundation Basic RiderCourse, which riders under 18 must complete
Motorcycle endorsements are set by engine displacement: W for 100 cc and up, Y for 50 to 99 cc, Z under 50 cc
Newly licensed riders under 18 may not carry passengers
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a securely fastened safety helmet
Riders must wear eye protection unless it has a fixed windshield
Titled and registered with the Motor Vehicle Division, and must carry liability insurance under the Mandatory Financial Responsibility Act
Carries a passenger only if it's designed for two
